article.headline: Super El Niño triggers storm surge across Southern United States this winter
article.summary: NOAA forecasts an active, storm-heavy winter pattern across the Southern U.S. driven by an 83% chance of a record-breaking Super El Niño.
article.body: Central equatorial Pacific water temperatures surpassed 2 degrees Celsius above normal during September, pushing current conditions into the high-stakes territory known as a Super El Niño. NOAA reports there is now an 83% likelihood that this season will become the strongest event of its kind since official record-keeping began in 1950, a notable jump from the 75% probability estimated just one month prior. This atmospheric shift essentially acts as a conveyor belt, extending the Pacific jet stream and directing a higher frequency of storms across the Southern Tier of the country. Residents from Southern California through the Southern Plains and into Florida should prepare for a particularly wet season as this climate phase takes hold. While the increased precipitation is expected to provide much-needed relief for drought-afflicted regions, NOAA officials have issued warnings that the influx of moisture onto dry, parched soil creates an elevated risk for destructive flash floods and sudden mudslides. Beyond the storm-prone South, the broader seasonal forecast points toward warmer-than-average temperatures settling over the majority of the remaining United States. Meteorological winter officially commences on December 1 and spans through the end of February, marking the period during which these El Niño-driven patterns are expected to exert their greatest influence. The event is defined by the El Niño-Southern Oscillation cycle, where significantly warmer water in the equatorial Pacific fundamentally alters global atmospheric circulation and shifts traditional storm tracks. Forecasters will continue to monitor whether sea surface temperatures remain at least 2 degrees above average for a three-month duration, the final threshold required to formally classify the season as a sustained Super El Niño event.

article.headline: Trump tells press secretary Katie Zacharia to reconsider role after five days
article.summary: President Trump is transitioning Katie Zacharia out of the White House press secretary role just five days after her initial appointment.
article.body:
Katie Zacharia’s tenure as White House press secretary lasted less than 15 minutes during her first public appearance on Tuesday, a debut that saw her take only three questions from reporters. Following a week of intense scrutiny, President Trump stated publicly that he told her she does not have to remain in the position if she does not want to, advising her that if he were in her shoes, he would reconsider the job. The White House has confirmed that Zacharia is currently transitioning out of her post.

The departure follows widespread questions regarding Zacharia’s professional background. According to the BBC, the primary point of contention involves her legal credentials; President Trump had originally introduced her as an attorney, despite the fact that Zacharia has never passed the bar exam and does not meet the legal definition for the title. Her week in the role was largely defined by fielding aggressive questioning from conservative news outlets regarding her preparedness and professional qualifications.

For the administration, the resignation highlights the ongoing difficulties in maintaining stable leadership within the communications office. The rapid turnover of a key spokesperson affects how the White House manages its messaging and interaction with the press corps. The scrutiny directed at Zacharia during her short time in office centers on the accuracy of the biographical information provided during her hiring process. While the White House has announced her transition out, there has been no formal timeline provided for the naming of a successor.

article.headline: Singapore Battles Toxic Haze as Prime Minister Targets Companies Behind Indonesia Fires
article.summary: Severe transboundary smoke from Indonesian wildfires has hit unhealthy air quality levels in Singapore, forcing business suspensions and government threats of prosecution.
article.body:
Visibility at Seletar Airport plummeted to levels requiring 16 flight diversions as smoke from massive wildfires in the Indonesian Kalimantan region descended on Singapore. The current haze, which first pushed air quality into unhealthy territory on Sept. 4, marks the most severe period of pollution in nearly three years. As the smog obscures the city-state's skyline, the impact is felt across every sector, from aviation and tourism to the daily routines of residents.

The widespread disruption carries significant economic and health implications for the population. Businesses reliant on outdoor activity are reporting sharp declines in patronage, while hotels such as Marina Bay Sands have moved to suspend specific outdoor experiences entirely. For many residents, the situation has become a matter of public health, prompting the government to begin mass mask distributions to support those most vulnerable to the persistent, acrid smoke.

Prime Minister Lawrence Wong confirmed on Thursday that his administration is actively identifying corporations potentially responsible for the forest and peatland fires. Under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act, Singapore is preparing to take legal action against these entities. While Indonesian officials have stated they remain capable of managing the crisis, Singaporean authorities are exploring both domestic legal enforcement and joint diplomatic measures to hold those responsible for the land-clearing practices accountable.

Government officials, including Minister for Digital Development and Information Josephine Teo, continue to monitor the situation as the city-state hosts major international events. While the exact timeline for clearing the atmosphere remains uncertain, Singaporean authorities are maintaining close contact with Indonesian counterparts to coordinate potential assistance.

article.headline: James Talarico defends moderate platform as tight Texas Senate race intensifies
article.summary: Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico faced direct questioning from voters on contentious policy issues during a televised CNN town hall Wednesday.
article.body:
James Talarico addressed a skeptical crowd including Republicans and independents during Wednesday’s event, directly answering questions regarding his past comments about God, his stance on abortion, and his approach to foreign aid. The town hall, which featured a young Republican activist who questioned Talarico's faith, highlighted the Democrat's attempt to bridge political divides in a state currently central to national Senate control. Talarico explicitly identified himself as a moderate candidate, promising to prioritize the needs of Texans over party allegiances.

This town hall matters as the race remains highly competitive, with recent polling placing Talarico in a narrow lead over his Republican opponent, Ken Paxton. For voters, the event provided a rare, unscripted look at how the Democratic nominee handles pressure on issues ranging from the military campaign in Gaza to reproductive rights. As Talarico seeks to appeal to a broad base, his ability to manage these encounters with undecided or critical voters could determine the outcome of the close contest.

According to The Guardian, Talarico engaged with voters such as Jodi Hunt, who challenged his pro-choice position through a Catholic lens. Talarico responded by framing abortion access as a public health issue while suggesting that the Bible remains silent on the topic. Host Erin Burnett noted at the beginning of the broadcast that Ken Paxton declined an invitation to appear alongside his challenger. Talarico also used the platform to position himself against the ultra-wealthy, designating them as a common enemy in his campaign rhetoric. The event, co-hosted by the Jubilee Media digital platform, marks a critical moment in the ongoing campaign as both candidates navigate the final stretches of their race for the Texas Senate seat.

article.headline: Eagles sign QB Joe Milton off Cowboys practice squad with Hurts sidelined
article.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles signed quarterback Joe Milton from the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad after starting QB Jalen Hurts was ruled out for Week 6 due to a superficial blood clot discovered after their London game against Jacksonville.
article.body:
Joe Milton joins the Eagles as backup depth after Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot, originally detected via ultrasound following the team's Saturday walkthrough before their game in London against the Jacksonville Jaguars. A follow-up ultrasound on Wednesday revealed movement in the small clot, leading the team to rule Hurts out for Week 6 against Carolina and determine the appropriate course of treatment.

With Hurts sidelined indefinitely, the Eagles need additional quarterback depth beyond Tanner McKee, who is expected to start Sunday against the Panthers. Milton spent the first five weeks of the season on Dallas' practice squad after being waived from the Cowboys' initial 53-man roster despite being drafted in the sixth round in 2024 by New England and traded to Dallas last year.

In his NFL career, Milton has appeared in five contests without starting a game. He completed 37-of-53 passes for 424 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions, while also rushing for 66 yards and a touchdown. Last season with Dallas, he went 15-of-24 for 183 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions across four games.

The Eagles, who have lost three straight games following a 2-0 start and fallen under .500 for the first time since 2021, will face the Panthers on Sunday. Cole Payton, a fifth-round pick in the 2026 draft from North Dakota State, remains the only other quarterback on the roster besides McKee.

article.headline: Prime Minister Mark Carney Warns Foreign Nations Against Meddling In Alberta Referendum
article.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney urges Albertans to vote in the upcoming October 19 referendum to ensure the integrity of the process against foreign interference.
article.body:
Leading figures in the separatist movement have traveled to the United States seeking assistance, with U.S. officials Scott Bessent and Howard Lutnik openly discussing Alberta as a potential partner or commenting on federal trade talks. Prime Minister Mark Carney told Global News that national security agencies are actively monitoring for covert foreign interference, though he declined to provide specific details regarding those investigations.    The upcoming vote is critical as it will decide whether Alberta initiates the legal process to hold a binding referendum on separation from Canada. The outcome of this decision carries significant weight for provincial politics, where the separatist debate has remained a dominant issue for more than a year. Carney emphasized that the most effective defense against outside influence is for residents to participate directly in the democratic process.

Speaking in Calgary, Carney stated that Ottawa has made it absolutely clear that foreign governments must remain uninvolved in domestic elections. He positioned voting as a fundamental duty for Albertans to ensure their own voices define the province's future. During his visit to the province, the Prime Minister highlighted recent federal investments, including the Pacific Link pipeline project intended for the British Columbia coast, as part of his administration's commitment to Alberta.

In addition to the separation question, ballots include five distinct immigration inquiries. While a rally in Calgary highlighted immigration as a central theme, Calgary Mayor Jeromy Farkas was the only official at the event to explicitly call for a "No" vote on the remaining nine items appearing on the ballot.

article.headline: False alarm at Miami University: gunfire reports turn out to be fireworks
article.summary: Miami University issued an active threat alert Thursday afternoon after reports of gunfire near McGuffey Hall, but police gave the all-clear after confirming the noise came from fireworks with no injuries.
article.body:
A loud noise outside McGuffey Hall sent Miami University into lockdown Thursday afternoon. Students in classrooms barricaded doors and called parents, with junior Nick Morre describing the moment as chaotic. "Everyone just started, like, barricading the doors," he said. "I was really scared for a good, like, 5 or 10 minutes."

The university's police department received reports of shots fired from a student in a classroom around 2 p.m., prompting a RedHawk Alert at 2:11 p.m. that told students to "run, hide, fight." Officers from Miami University Police, Oxford Police Department, and Butler County Sheriff's Office responded within a minute. After speaking with witnesses, they determined the noise sounded more like fireworks. The Butler County Sheriff's Office later confirmed it was fireworks, not gunfire.

Police found no evidence of gunfire or injuries after searching McGuffey Hall and the surrounding area. The university gave the all-clear shortly before 2:40 p.m., declaring it safe to resume daily activities. However, the university cancelled in-person classes for the rest of the evening. University police emphasized that student safety remains their top priority, with the incident leaving many students visibly shaken despite the absence of any actual threat.

article.headline: Duchess of Sussex Relaunches Public UK Appearances with Nottingham Charity Away Day
article.summary: Meghan Markle returned to Nottingham for her first joint UK engagement in years, visiting local charities and meeting with volunteers.
article.body:
The atmosphere in Nottingham mirrored the couple's first visit in 2017, with the Duchess of Sussex engaging in informal activities such as baking cupcakes, preparing West African food, and playing basketball. This event, which involved accepting flowers and greeting crowds, marked the first time the Duchess participated in a public outing of this nature on British soil in several years. Observers noted that the Duchess displayed a familiar American confidence while interacting with a largely youthful crowd, mostly aged under 30.

This return to public engagement signifies a move by the Duke and Duchess to carry out their own events on their own terms. While the Royal Family classifies the pair as private citizens without official royal status, the visit highlighted the Sussexes' continued ability to draw public interest. The event served as a sharp contrast to the official duties undertaken by King Charles III, who was simultaneously present at the ceremonial opening of the Senedd in Cardiff.

Reports indicate that the Sussexes do not consider themselves bound by previous agreements regarding their royal roles, with sources suggesting the couple never consented to being fully excluded from public life. The visit occurred following the couple's return to the UK with their children, Archie and Lilibet. While Buckingham Palace maintains that the Duke and Duchess operate independently, their actions remain a source of complexity for the monarchy. The visit is framed by the couple as they establish their own path, picking up activities that resemble their previous royal engagements but without the associated formal duties.

article.headline: Benfica Routs Celtic 4-1 as Scottish Champions Struggle in Europe League
article.summary: Celtic remain winless in the Europa League after suffering a 4-1 defeat away to Benfica in Lisbon.
article.body:
Celtic were effectively out of the contest by halftime, trailing 3-0 after a series of defensive errors left the Scottish side facing a mountain to climb. The visitors handed Benfica an early lead just four minutes into the match when Dane Murray conceded a penalty, which Jhon Duran converted. Alexander Bah added a second before Jhon Duran scored his brace, leaving Celtic 34th out of 36 teams in the competition standings after two matches. While Camilo Duran pulled a goal back for the visitors after the break, Vangelis Pavlidis eventually sealed the comprehensive win for the hosts with a late fourth goal.

The loss marks Celtic's fourth defeat in their past five matches across all competitions. For manager Martin O'Neill, the result underscores a difficult start to the European campaign, as his side has now lost both of their opening group matches. Despite the outcome, O'Neill expressed optimism regarding his team's second-half performance, insisting that the attacking display provides a foundation for the remainder of the league phase.

According to the BBC, the scoreline accurately reflected the disparity between the two sides, as Benfica dominated possession and hit the woodwork multiple times throughout the encounter. Captain Callum McGregor acknowledged that unforced errors were the primary cause of the collapse, noting that the team failed to manage the ball effectively at the top level. Although Celtic managed to create several chances in the second half, they were consistently punished by a clinical Benfica side that remained superior in both halves of play. The defeat leaves Celtic searching for their first points of the European season as they prepare for upcoming fixtures.

article.headline: Two-time World Series champion Miguel Rojas retires following Dodgers championship series loss
article.summary: Veteran infielder Miguel Rojas announced his retirement after the Los Angeles Dodgers were eliminated from the National League Championship Series on Thursday.
article.body:
The 37-year-old infielder broke the news to his teammates inside the clubhouse immediately following the Dodgers' Game 4 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers. Reflecting on his tenure in Los Angeles, Rojas told reporters that his time with the team over the last four years changed his life as he prepares to move on to the next chapter of his career. 

For baseball fans and the organization, the departure of the veteran signals the end of a 13-year career in the Major Leagues. His exit leaves a gap in the Dodgers' lineup, where he was a key contributor during back-to-back championship runs in 2024 and 2025. Beyond his defensive reliability, Rojas etched his name into team history by hitting a ninth-inning game-tying home run during Game 7 of the 2024 World Series against the Toronto Blue Jays. 

According to Sportsnet, Rojas finished his career with 1,401 appearances, recording a slash line of .260/.313/.363 and a .677 OPS. His career path began and ended in a Dodgers uniform, with a middle stretch spent playing for the Miami Marlins. 

While his playing days have concluded, industry speculation suggests his involvement in the sport may continue. Reports from MLB Trade Rumors indicate that Rojas could transition into a coaching or managerial role in the near future, citing potential interest from teams seeking his experience on the field.

Raty previously helped the Abbotsford Canucks secure the Calder Cup in 2025 and has recorded 14 goals and 29 points across 118 career NHL games. His professional experience includes stints with the New York Islanders and the Vancouver Canucks, the latter of which he joined in 2023. This season, Raty averaged 10:10 of ice time over four games with Vancouver, contributing one goal. 

This roster shift provides the Vancouver Canucks with two new players to bolster their overall depth as the season progresses. General Manager Ryan Johnson noted the organization's intent to continue finding ways to improve the group by working with these new young prospects. The move marks a significant change for both teams as they adjust their forward depth charts.

Jacob Quillan joins the Canucks after recording three points in 24 NHL games with Toronto and appearing in 114 games for the Toronto Marlies. He is credited with a Calder Cup title from his time with the Marlies. Brandon Buhr also moves to Vancouver, bringing his experience from the NCAA, where he recorded 88 points over 116 games split between Clarkson University and Union College. article.headline: Ballina woman scoops $100 million Powerball jackpot with single winning ticket
article.summary: A woman from Ballina, NSW, became Australia's third-biggest lottery winner after matching all seven numbers and the Powerball on Thursday night, crediting the win to a sign from a recently deceased family member.
article.body:
The Ballina resident's initial reaction to the news was disbelief. "Bloody hell! Is this my cousin pranking me?" she said after receiving a call from Powerball operator The Lott confirming her division one win. She was the only person in Australia to correctly match all seven numbers plus the Powerball number on Thursday night.

The winner's $100 million jackpot places her among Australia's largest lottery winners in history, ranking as the country's third-biggest prize. She purchased her entry online, adding to the randomness of her windfall.

The woman attributed her extraordinary fortune to spiritual intervention. "We recently had a death in the family, and I think it's a sign from them; they're so looking after me!" she explained. She reported experiencing signs throughout the day, describing objects moving and items waving in the wind as confirmations of the family member's involvement in her luck.

Her immediate plans center on practical and generous use of the funds. She intends to pay off her mortgage and assist family members in need. "This will help a lot of people. Not just me but lots of family members," she said. Her celebration will be modest by comparison: "Celebrating with breakfast in bed tomorrow - scrambled eggs and bacon for me!"
